questions.q: What does a NetFlow record actually contain?
options: Metadata about a traffic flow — source/destination IP and port, protocol, duration, and byte/packet counts, but not the payload content
The complete payload contents of every packet in the flow
Only the destination IP address, with no other fields
A full packet capture saved in a different file format
questions.explain: NetFlow records capture the 5-tuple plus counters and duration — metadata only, never the actual payload.

questions.q: Why is flow data cheaper to store and analyze at scale than full packet capture?
options: Each flow record is a small, compact line of metadata, while full capture stores every header and payload byte for every packet
Flow data is stored on a different, inherently cheaper type of hard drive
Flow records are only generated once per day instead of continuously
There is no real cost difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: A flow record's small size is exactly what lets a collector retain months of history where full capture would fill the same space in a day.

questions.q: Which organization originally developed NetFlow, and what is it now the basis for?
options: Cisco; it's now the basis for the open IPFIX standard
A W3C working group; it's now a deprecated HTML standard
Wireshark's developers; it's now a built-in Wireshark-only feature
The IETF, with no relationship to any other standard
questions.explain: NetFlow originated at Cisco in the mid-1990s and evolved into the open, multi-vendor IPFIX standard.

questions.q: What does the 5-tuple in a flow record consist of?
options: Source IP, destination IP, source port, destination port, and protocol
Source IP, destination IP, and nothing else
Five separate IP addresses involved in a connection
The five busiest ports on a given device
questions.explain: The 5-tuple is what defines a flow: source/destination IP, source/destination port, and protocol.

questions.q: Based on a flow record alone, what can a SOC NOT determine about a given transfer?
options: What the actual payload content of the traffic was
How many bytes were transferred
Which source and destination IP were involved
How long the flow lasted
questions.explain: NetFlow never records payload content — only metadata like IPs, ports, protocol, duration, and counts.
